cards.title: Single-Task Seasons Beat Multitasking Marathons
cards.insight: Productivity peaks when you align your energy with seasonal or project-based cycles rather than juggling parallel priorities. Batch similar work, establish clear season boundaries, and signal when you're switching focus modes.
cards.takeaway: Declare one "primary focus" per quarter; communicate it to your team so context-switching expectations reset.

cards.title: Friction Points Are Hidden Productivity Leaks
cards.insight: Repeated small obstacles—authentication delays, notification interruptions, unclear workflows—accumulate into massive time loss. Often the biggest gains come from removing one friction point, not adding new tools.
cards.takeaway: Track three tasks that annoyed you this week; systematically eliminate the friction from the one causing most delay.

cards.title: Recovery Time Is Peak Performance Planning
cards.insight: The gap between intense work blocks and real rest determines sustainable output. Rushing from one task to another without transition depletes cognitive reserves; spacing allows pattern recognition and creative insight.
cards.takeaway: After deep work sessions, enforce 15-minute "transition" blocks with no email or new tasks—let your mind settle.

cards.title: Clear Exit Criteria Beat Endless Refinement
cards.insight: Ambiguous finish lines invite perfectionism and scope creep, killing momentum. Defining success upfront—what "done" means, what version 1.0 includes—creates psychological closure and frees you to move forward.
cards.takeaway: Before starting any project, write three acceptance criteria and share them with a colleague; revisit only if requirements genuinely shift.
